title.narrative: Hazard Risk Mitigation & Emergency Preparedness Project

description.narrative: The overall objective of the Hazard Risk Mitigation and Emergency Preparedness Project is to assist the Government in reducing the environmental, social, and economic vulnerability to natural disasters, and catastrophic mining accidental spills of pollutants, by strengthening the institutional and technical capacity for disaster management and emergency response, through upgrading communication and information systems; implementing specific risk reduction investments for floods, landslides and earthquakes; improving the safety of selected water-retention dams; and, improving, on a pilot basis, the management and safety of tailings dams, and waste dump facilities. Through its components the project will: 1) strengthen and enhance the capacity of Romanian authorities to better prepare for, respond to, and recover from natural or man-made disasters, through modernization of information technology and communications systems, public awareness and preparedness, and technical feasibility work, and institutional framework for launching of the Romanian Catastrophe Insurance Program; 2) reduce the seismic vulnerability of priority technical and social infrastructure, through the retrofitting of key structures, and institutional strengthening; 3) reduce flood risk and vulnerability in critical areas in Romania, to improve safety of large and small dams, in order for these to function as designed, and, to map and model the risk of landslides, so as to reduce losses, providing better land use planning tools; 4) reduce the risk of water and soil contamination, and loss of human and aquatic life from catastrophic mining accidental spills of pollutants. The global environmental objective is to demonstrate, and provide replication for the reduction of catastrophic accidental spills of trans-boundary pollution loads, from mine operations flowing into the Danube and Black Sea basins. Finally, Project management unit costs will be financed, to be established in the respective ministries responsible for each related component.

The overall objective of the project is to assist the Government of Romania in reducing the environmental, social, and economic vulnerability to natural disasters and catastrophic mining accidental spills of pollutants through: (i) strengthening the institutional and technical capacity for disaster management and emergency response through upgrading communication and information systems; (ii) implementing specific risk reduction investments for floods, landslides and earthquakes; (iii) improving the safety of selected water-retention dams; and (iv) improving on a pilot basis the management and safety of tailings dams and waste dump facilities.

title.narrative: Improved expertise and practice in safe management of mine waste, leading to higher risk awareness and awareness of valued environmental components and potental negative impacts

baseline.value: Fragmented, dispersed and inconsistent national approach and awareness of environmental dimension of mine waste, not consolidatednational policy or management efforts.

comment.narrative: This indicator is formally no longer kept after the restructuring in 2010, but was not dropped from the system; the team thuscontinues to monitor and report on the status.

target.value: Integrated monitoring and emergency warning system implemented, operated / maintained by Romanian public agencies and used byRomanian mining / environment experts

comment.narrative: Completion expected after project closure, the finalization of activities will be financed from saved Govt contributions.

actual.value: The core modules of an integrated monitoring and emergency warning system are under installation; operation and maintenancearrangements by have been agreed between and clearly assigned to Romanian public agencies.

comment.narrative: Tendering for supply and installation of integrated monitoring and emergency warning system compelted in April 2012, installationis in progress and expected to be completed July / August 2012.

title.narrative: Improved dam safety in the seven selected priority structures.

baseline.value: 55 dams are at risk and need rehabilitation, of which 13 high risk dams were selected for improving their safety, to protect about300,000 people living in their neighborhood.

target.value: The risk of dam failure removed and improved safety in place for seven of the 13 critical dams selected and only 60% of people atrisk in the project areas protected.

actual.value: Works contracts for six dams (protecting about 195,000 people) have been completed, while the last contract is beingcompleted. About 53% of people at risk in the project area (represented by the 13 dams selected at project outset) protected,representing 85% of target, achieved.

comment.narrative: Implementation of the works contract to increase safety of Dridu dam is under completion.

title.narrative: Improved dam safety in the seven selected priority structures.

baseline.value: 55 dams are at risk and need rehabilitation, of which 13 high risk dams were selected for improving their safety, to protect about300,000 people living in their neighborhood.

target.value: The risk of dam failure removed and improved safety in place for seven critical dams selected.

comment.narrative: The target was revised and reduced from 13 dams to 7 dams through the project restructuring approved in August 2010.

actual.value: Work contracts for increasing the safety of dams have been completed, improving the safety of seven dams and removing the risk oftheir failure.

comment.narrative: Target met 100%. About 222,700 people are now protected against dam accidents/failure.

title.narrative: The risk of flood in 10 high priority areas was reduced through flood protection investments.

baseline.value: About 30,000 people live and work in the 10 areas exposed to flood risk due to river flooding.

target.value: Flood protection works completed in all 10 critical locations included in the investment program and no people at risk in theproject areas

comment.narrative: Target met. The target was revised and reduced from 11 to 10 flood protection sites through the project restructuring approved inAugust 2010.

actual.value: Contruction works for flood protection completed in all 10 sites and no people at risk in the project area.

comment.narrative: Target met since 2009. Protection against floods was provided to over 43,500 people.

title.narrative: Establishment and maintenance of an integrated knowledge base about transboundary impacts of mine-induced pollution in the Danube and Black Sea basins.

baseline.value: Limited appreciation of the hazards associated with tailings management facilities, especially on policy- & decision making levels.

target.value: Environmental monitoring systems installed and operational in all project sites, linked with other closed mines and high risk spots

comment.narrative: System will be almost complete but not yet operational. The completion will by financed by the Govt. Operation will be sharedbetween NAMR and Conversmin, with the former managing the hardware core (servers) and the latter providing both input data andconstituting the main Client for the system's outputs.

actual.value: Environmental monitoring systems contracted and under implementation (installation being carried out). Operation and maintenancearrangements agreed between RO public agencies. Finalization and putting into operation expected in July 2012 (completion will befinanced by RO Govt)

comment.narrative: The system will be installed at one pilot site only due to budget constraints. However, due to the modular and expandablecharacterof the system, and the Internet-based access to data, a swift expansion and widespread use is expected.

title.narrative: Reduced earthquake risk for at least 40 priority public facilities through seismic retrofitting.

baseline.value: More than 350 public facilities are at risk, of which 68 high risk facilities (w hich normally host over 27,000 people and serviceover 2 million people) were se lected for seismic retrofitting.

target.value: The risk of collapse of at least 40 critical public buildings in case of a seismic event removed and they will be safelyoperational.

comment.narrative: Target substantially met and likely to be met before project closing. Target revised and reduced from 50 buildings to 40buildingsthrough the project restructuring approved in August 2010.

actual.value: Seismic retrofitting of 39 public buildings completed and 2 more buildings with seismic retrofitting near completion, will becompleted by June 30, 2012. The risk of collapse of these buildings in case of a seismic event removed and they will be safelyoperational.

comment.narrative: Seismic retrofitting of two more buildings will be completed by the Closing Date enabling meeting the target. The target met 97.5%.

title.narrative: Reduced earthquake risk for at least 50 priority public facilities through seismic retrofitting.

baseline.value: More than 350 public facilities are at risk, of which 68 high risk facilities (w hich normally host over 27,000 people and serviceover 2 million people) were se lected for seismic retrofitting.

target.value: The risk of collapse of at least 40 critical public buildings in case of a seismic event removed and they will be safelyoperational.

actual.value: Seismic retrofitting of 38 buildings completed and 26 buildings have been returned into functional conditions.

comment.narrative: The target almost met and will be exceeded with the project extension.

title.narrative: Increased transboundary cooperation for integrated water resources management

baseline.value: No formal forum to foster transboundary cooperation.

target.value: Proposal is drafted for continued initiatives / projects for transboundary water resources management

actual.value: Throughout project implementation regular meetings of international task force; continued international dialogue on TMF safety

comment.narrative: No further action required.

title.narrative: Increased transboundary cooperation for integrated water resources management

baseline.value: No formal forum to foster transboundary cooperation.

target.value: Proposal is drafted for continued initiatives / projects for transboundary water resources management

comment.narrative: Will remain unchanged at project closure.

actual.value: Under the project close personal and professional ties were established between Romanian and riparian stakeholders, which willcontinue to works towards improved transboundary water resources management.

comment.narrative: The benefits and necessity of a transboundary dialogue have been widely recognized and strengthened during the projectimplementation period and are now generally accepted by both RO and riparian Governments. No further action required.

title.narrative: Improved factors in safety in tailings facilities and increased standards in risk awareness, assessment, management and emergency preparedness.

baseline.value: Performance standards with clear technical criteria to be developed within first year of project implementation.

target.value: At least 70% of performance standards achieved, which are used in international good practice.

actual.value: The target has been substantially with about 65% of performance standards achieved following the project activities complementedbythe Govt. programs and improved engineering standards. Consolidation with national emergency services was achieved.

comment.narrative: No change expected.

title.narrative: Improved factors in safety in tailings facilities and increased standards in risk awareness, assessment, management and emergency preparedness.

baseline.value: Performance standards with clear technical criteria to be developed within first year of project implementation.

target.value: Management and maintenance achieved according to best available techniques and internationally accepted performance standardsachieved for at least 70% of the inventory of mine waste facilities.

comment.narrative: Combined with the process of EU alignment the upgraded performance standards established under the project are expected to reach100% coverage, meaning that all mine waste management activities in RO will be carried out according to BAT (best availabletechniques).

actual.value: The use of performance standards has been further consolidated, with the target value of 70% of teh country's portfolio achievedoreven surpassed. Romanian public agencies have taken over standards and practices developed under the project on a broad front andare consistently implementing the good practice approach and techniques promoted by the project.

comment.narrative: Objective met.

title.narrative: Increased adoption of best mine waste management practices throughout the Tisza Basin and Danube basins.

target.value: Formal adoption of guidelines in context of international good practice and wider legislative environment (EU).

actual.value: The guidelines for best mine waste management developed under the project adopted by the Romanian public agencies in charge withmine closure and waste management as part of alignment to the EU mine waste directive.

title.narrative: Gradual reduction in probability and negative consequences of severe accidental spills of mining-related pollutants into the hydrological network of the Tisza Basin.

baseline.value: Tailing facilities are not safe and at least four objects are prone to catastrop hic accidents. Quantitative indicators to bedetermined during field surveys.

target.value: The residual accident risk for the sites remediated by the project is considered very low (estd. less than 1 event per 1,000years). A similar trend has significantly reduced the country's overall portfolio, due to Government-funded programs motivated byEU alignment and fostered by the project's technical expertise.

comment.narrative: Target number of remediated sites was significantly exceeded due to savings in unit cost of works. Significant knowledge transferoccurred between project and Govt agencies.

actual.value: The target has been substantially met with the probability of accidental spills at the project sites significantly reduced(estimated to less than 1 significant event per 100 years), through project activities complemented by the Govt programs and EUalignment.

comment.narrative: Remediation works at the new high risk sites were completed since November 2011.
